citeAs: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang (2024). Dissecting Dissonance: Benchmarking Large Multimodal Models Against Self-Contradictory Instructions. arXiv:2408.01091.
creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Fudan University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory)
description: The Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) benchmark evaluates the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to recognize conflicting commands. It comprises 20,000 conflicts evenly distributed between language-language (L-L) and vision-language (V-L) paradigms, spanning 8 tasks (RuleConflict, AttributeConflict, ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict, OCRConflict, FigureConflict, GeometricConflict, SemanticConflict). It is constructed using an automatic dataset creation framework called AutoCreate, which leverages programs and large language models.
name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) benchmark - self-contradictory subset
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: LLM evaluation agents were validated against human expert evaluations. Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate were calculated between LLM agent and human expert evaluations on vision-language conflicts: GPT-4V replies: Spearman's ρ=0.881, Concordance=94%; LLaVA-1.5 replies: Spearman's ρ=0.999, Concordance=99%; Gemini replies: Spearman's ρ=0.854, Concordance=97%. GPT-4 evaluation results showed overall discrepancy within 5% compared to human experts.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Human experts (in-house); LLM-based evaluation agents (GPT-4, ChatGPT, ChatGLM) used for automated quality checking and evaluation alignment verification.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts manually checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset. For evaluation, human experts assessed whether LMM replies successfully identified conflicts. A uniform prompt for all tasks was designed to prompt LLMs as evaluation agents. Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate were calculated to measure evaluation consistency between humans and LLM agents (GPT-4 showed 0.881 Spearman's ρ and 94% concordance with human experts for GPT-4V replies).
rai:dataBiases: The dataset uses synthetic data generated by LLMs, which may inherit biases from the underlying LLMs used in AutoCreate. SemanticConflict relies on ImageNet, which has known class distribution and demographic biases. The paper notes that LLM-generated questions may have ambiguous answers even with explicit emphasis on uniqueness (addressed by an LLM agent filter for ForbbidenConflict). The dataset is constructed to cover a wide range of instruction forms, complexities, and scopes to mitigate coverage bias.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed using AutoCreate, a novel automatic dataset creation framework that leverages programs and large language models. AutoCreate starts from manually input seeds and maintains a seed pool. During each cycle, it includes two branches (language and vision), each consisting of a generator, decorator, and cleaner. The generator creates initial language/vision data, the decorator creates self-contradictions in the generated data, and the cleaner removes data that does not meet quality standards. Both human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset. For SemanticConflict, images are retrieved from the ImageNet dataset.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: (1) manually crafted seed prompts and instruction pairs; (2) LLM-generated text (contexts, questions, descriptions, fictional object attributes, exclusive instruction pairs, forbidden word lists); (3) ImageNet dataset (imagenet-1k validation set) for SemanticConflict images; (4) programmatically generated geometric shape images and chart/figure images for GeometricConflict and FigureConflict.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms; more modalities are planned for future inclusion. No fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree. No detailed study is provided on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For FigureConflict, the largest value in the data dictionary is changed to the smallest value to create a conflict between the figure and the text description. For SemanticConflict, the correct ImageNet class label in questions is substituted with a similar but different object. For GeometricConflict, two attributes in the text description are exchanged to refer to a non-existent object. For OCRConflict, images vary in font, size, and color to augment diversity. For FigureConflict, charts are plotted with random choices for font, size, color, and other style options.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A Cleaner component in AutoCreate removes data that does not meet quality standards. Human experts rigorously checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset. For SCI-Core and SCI-Base, subsets are selected manually with sizes of 1% and 10% of SCI-All respectively. For ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict, and OCRConflict, extra effort is applied to guarantee diversity when used in SCI-Core. An LLM agent is used to judge whether generated questions have unique answers (for ForbbidenConflict).
rai:dataSocialImpact: The SCI benchmark provides researchers and practitioners with a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies. The AutoCreate framework facilitates the creation of diverse instruction datasets, promoting inclusivity in AI research. The CaP approach integrates external cognition into multimodal models, enhancing context-aware understanding. By improving dissonance detection, the approach boosts LMM performance and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems, essential for societal integration. The work is particularly relevant for protecting language beginners and vulnerable populations who may be misled by conflicting instructions.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to detect and recognize self-contradictory or conflicting instructions in both language-language and vision-language paradigms. Benchmarking LMM self-awareness and meta-cognition. Assessing prompting techniques (e.g., Cognitive Awakening Prompting) for improving dissonance detection. Advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies, particularly for language beginners and vulnerable populations who may encounter conflicting instructions.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large Language Models (LLMs) used throughout the AutoCreate pipeline for data generation, decoration, and quality checking. GPT-4 used as an evaluation agent to assess whether LMM replies identify conflicts. ChatGPT and ChatGLM also used as evaluation agents. ImageNet labels and image retrieval used for SemanticConflict generation.

null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
